To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the design of biodegradable/clearable inorganic nanoparticles is of crucial importance for their biological applications, and that a comprehensive understanding of the metabolic performance of these inorganic nanostructures in the body is necessary for advancing clinical translation and expanding their biological applications in diagnosis.

we have developed a series of biodegradable inorganic nanoparticles with tunability in terms of size, morphology, and surface chemistry for biomedical applications, and that we have demonstrated that the biodegradability of the inorganic nanoparticles is dependent on their size, morphology, composition, and surface chemistry, and can be modulated by the introduction of specific functional groups to their surface, which has enabled the in vivo metabolism of the inorganic nanomaterials and their subsequent excretion from the body.
we have developed a novel class of biodegradable and clearable inorganic nanomaterials that can be used as theranostics for the diagnosis and treatment of cancer.

the synthesis of inorganic nanoparticles with tunability in size, shape, surface chemistry, doping strategy, and intrinsic responsiveness to the tumor microenvironment.
developing new nanomaterials for biomedical applications, including drug delivery and imaging.
the development of inorganic nanoparticles for biomedical applications.

the development of biodegradable and clearable inorganic nanomaterials is a rapidly growing field with tremendous potential for future biomedical applications.
biodegradable and/or clearable inorganic nanomaterials hold great promise to address the toxicity concerns of inorganic nanoparticles, and thus to expand their biomedical applications.
the biodegradability or clearance of the inorganic nanoparticles can be modulated through the control of their size, shape, surface chemistry and composition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design of biodegradable/clearable inorganic nanoparticles is a multifaceted problem that requires a deep understanding of the material properties and the biological environment.

the design and synthesis of biodegradable and clearable inorganic nanomaterials with tunable and controllable metabolic performance is of crucial importance for the advancement of clinical translation and expanding biological applications in disease diagnostics and therapeutics.
the design of biodegradable inorganic nanoparticles has been greatly improved, which has led to their clinical applications for disease diagnosis.

the metabolic behavior of these biodegradable and clearable inorganic nanomaterials in the body is highly complex.

the design of biodegradable inorganic nanoparticles with tunability of size, morphology, and surface chemistry, as well as their metabolic performance in vivo, are of paramount importance for their clinical translation.
